  "text": "Field experiments were carried out in four inland water bodies to study how much dissolved organic carbon phytoplankton release. Researchers added a radioactive form of carbon to the water and measured how much ended up in the cells by collecting them on fine filters. The remaining dissolved carbon was separated by bubbling air through the water at low acidity, then dried on metal plates to count the radioactivity. The proportion of carbon released as dissolved material grew larger with depth in the sunlit layer and also showed a rise near the surface when light was very intense, a condition that suppresses photosynthesis.
